concept.name: Bearish harami
concept.definition: A two-candlestick pattern appearing after an uptrend: an unusually large white body is followed by a small black body contained entirely within it. Technical analysts read it as a potential bearish reversal sign, interpreting the sudden contraction of range as buying pressure drying up; it is the bearish mirror of the bullish harami and requires confirmation.
concept.intuition: After a big up day, the market stalls into a tiny down day nested inside the prior body, suggesting the rally's energy is spent and sellers are probing.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long white body; candle 2 is a small black body with both open and close inside body 1's open-close range. A doji second candle turns it into a (bearish) harami cross; a third candle closing below body 1 converts it into the three inside down confirmation pattern.
concept.failure_modes: In persistent uptrends the small contained candle is usually just consolidation, and the trend resumes higher. Its low standalone reliability means unconfirmed bearish harami shorts fail frequently.
concept.misconceptions: It is not a confirmed top; the conventional use waits for price to break below the first candle's body. Only the second candle's body must be contained, not its shadows.
concept.example: In an uptrend, a stock prints a long white candle (65.00 to 68.00), then a small black candle opening at 67.60 and closing at 67.10. Bears treat a subsequent close below 65.00 (a three inside down) as confirmation of the reversal warning.
